Name of the Surah

• It is called al-ʿĀdiyāt (The Charging Steeds), because it opens with God's oath by al-ʿādiyāt, which are the horses that run in jihad in the way of God.

Among the Objectives of the Surah

• To make clear man's ingratitude and denial of God's blessings upon him, and his intense love of wealth, and to admonish people about what lies ahead of them of reckoning for their deeds after death; as a reminder for the believer and a warning for the one who denies.

[The Exegesis]

God Most High swears by the horses that run in His way toward the enemy, when the sound of their breathing becomes audible from the speed of their running. It is not permissible for a created being to swear except by God, for swearing by other than God is shirk (association of partners with God).
By the swift horses whose hooves strike sparks of fire from their hardness, because of the intensity of their running.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 100, verse 3:

"By the warhorses that charge at dawn with their riders against the enemy."
Thus, by this running, they stirred up dust.

The Qur'anic verse is ﴿فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعًا﴾ in its standard form, but the passage given reads: "فتوسَّطن بركبانهن جموع الأعداء."

Translation:

"They [the swift war-horses] penetrated with their riders into the midst of the masses of the enemy."

**Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 100, verse 9:**

Does not man know what awaits him when God brings forth the dead from their graves for reckoning and recompense?
And what was concealed within the breasts is brought out, of good or of evil.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 100, verse 11:

Indeed, their Lord, concerning them and their deeds, on that Day, is All-Aware. Nothing of that is hidden from Him.
